visual.detailed_description: Three-panel color clinical photograph figure (labels A, B, C printed at the lower left of each panel) showing patchy erythematous plaques on the neck and upper chest, the face and neck, and the arm. Panel A: Three-quarter side view of the neck and upper chest of a person in a dark top with the hair pulled up and the chin turned toward the shoulder. Confluent red-brown patches cover the neck and extend onto the upper chest and shoulder, with scattered smaller red-brown spots around the edges of the patches. The background is a plain pale wall. No printed text, arrows or scale are visible. Individual pustules are not clearly resolvable at this resolution. Panel B: Frontal close view of the lower two thirds of a face with the eyes closed, nose and closed lips at the centre, a dark top below. Scattered small red-brown spots are visible over the cheeks, forehead edge and neck/chin area, with larger confluent patches on the lower neck at the bottom of the frame. The background is a plain pale wall. No printed text, arrows or scale are visible. Panel C: Close view of an arm (elbow and forearm region) with several round to annular erythematous plaques of varying size, some with a paler scaly rim and tiny crusted or pustule-like points near the edges, on a lighter brown skin background. A dark cloth and a blue background object are at the right and lower edge. No printed text, arrows or scale are visible.

visual.general_description: Three-panel color clinical photograph figure (labels A, B, C printed at the lower left of each panel) showing crusted ulcers on the jaw with a red chest band, crusted ulcers on the lips and chin, and extensive erythematous patches on both arms.
visual.detailed_description: Three-panel color clinical photograph figure (labels A, B, C printed at the lower left of each panel) showing crusted ulcers on the jaw with a red chest band, crusted ulcers on the lips and chin, and extensive erythematous patches on both arms. Panel A: Side view of the lower face, jaw and neck turned to one side. Several round lesions with a brown-yellow crusted or necrotic centre and a red rim lie along the jaw and cheek, the largest near the jaw angle, with smaller ones nearby. A thin red serpiginous band runs down the neck onto the upper chest/shoulder, and skin between lesions is brown with mild scattered spots. A plain wall is the background. No printed text, arrows or scale are visible. Panel B: Close frontal view of the mouth and chin with the nose tip at the top edge. A crusted dark-brown ulcerated lesion with a red margin sits on the upper lip at the midline and another larger crusted ulcer on the lower lip/chin below the lower lip; a third round crusted ulcer lies at the left edge of the chin/cheek. The surrounding skin is brown with fine mottling. No printed text, arrows or scale are visible. Panel C: A person lying on white hospital bedding, both arms extended downward in front of the chest. Extensive confluent red to orange-red patches with annular and geographic borders and paler skin islands cover both upper arms and forearms and the neck and upper chest. A clear adhesive dressing with a handwritten, illegible note secures a cannula on the right-hand arm of the image, and a hospital wrist band is at the lower left. Part of the chin and hair is at the top edge. No panel-internal printed text is legible.

visual.general_description: Two-panel figure with printed labels "A Flare up (before spesolimab)" and "B After the biological treatment (Spesolimab)", each panel containing two color clinical photographs of skin.
visual.detailed_description: Two-panel figure with printed labels "A Flare up (before spesolimab)" and "B After the biological treatment (Spesolimab)", each panel containing two color clinical photographs of skin. Panel A: Two adjacent color photographs under the printed label "Flare up (before spesolimab)". The left photograph shows skin with several round to annular erythematous plaques with grey-white scaly or violaceous centres and raised pink borders. The right photograph shows the neck and hairline area with many small coalescing pink-red plaques and papules. No scale or other printed text is visible. Panel B: Two adjacent color photographs under the printed label "After the biological treatment (Spesolimab)". The left photograph shows both forearms resting in front of the lap with mostly even tan skin and faint residual pigment change, in a clinic room with a blue chair. The right photograph shows the upper chest and torso with a few faint pink patches and otherwise even skin; a dark garment frames the chest. No red plaques or pustules are clearly visible. No other printed text is visible.
